Eval 4 (Add Workflow) is completely non-discriminating: both with_skill and without_skill scored 4/4 (100%). Adding a workflow to an existing skill is simple enough that general knowledge suffices.
Eval 5 (Update Skill - fix gaps) is also non-discriminating: both scored 3/3 (100%). Detecting missing Examples and Success Criteria sections requires reading, not specialized knowledge.

Eval 2 (Vague CreateSkill) is the most discriminating eval: with_skill 2/2 (100%) vs without_skill 0/2 (0%). SkillForge's CreateSkill workflow explicitly interviews the user before creating files; without it, the agent plowed ahead without clarifying.

Eval 3 (Internal workflow) is highly discriminating: with_skill 4/4 (100%) vs without_skill 2/4 (50%). The 'SSH handler NOT in routing table' and 'read-and-follow instruction' assertions are SkillForge-specific conventions that a baseline agent wouldn't know.

Assertion 'Agent ran ValidateSkill.ts' fails in BOTH configurations (eval 6). The with_skill agent noted ValidateSkill.ts expects skills under $PAI_DIR/skills/ but the test-target was at a non-standard workspace path. This assertion is structurally unfair for workspace-based evals.

Assertion 'Agent invoked run_loop.py or run_eval.py' fails for with_skill eval 7 ('No transcript available') — the OptimizeDescription subagent ran too long and didn't produce a transcript. Without-skill also fails since it doesn't know about these scripts.

Eval 7 has a reverse-discriminating assertion: 'Description differs from original' PASSES without_skill but FAILS with_skill. The with_skill agent correctly generated eval queries and attempted run_loop.py but didn't complete, while the without_skill agent simply rewrote the description directly.

Tools/ directory existence (eval 1) is a clean discriminator: with_skill passes, without_skill fails. SkillForge's CreateSkill standard structure includes Tools/; baseline agents create Workflows/ but not Tools/.

'USE WHEN clause' presence (eval 1) is non-discriminating — both pass. The model has internalized USE WHEN as a skill convention even without SkillForge guidance. This may indicate USE WHEN is already in the model's training data.

Eval 8 'Domain-specific queries' discriminates: with_skill agent generated domain-specific eval queries via OptimizeDescription workflow; without_skill agent had no concept of generating eval queries and only modified the description.

Timing and token data are all zeros across all runs. Self-reported metrics.json from subagents did not capture actual timing. This means time/token tradeoff analysis is not possible for this benchmark.

The with_skill stddev (0.186) is much lower than without_skill stddev (0.3355), suggesting the skill provides more consistent results across diverse tasks. Without the skill, performance is highly variable by eval type.
Eval 6 (Refactor) scores identically in both configs (3/4, 75%) — the only failure is the ValidateSkill.ts assertion. The rename-and-update-references task is well within baseline capability.

OptimizeDescription evals (7, 8) are the weakest area: with_skill averages 75% vs without_skill 50%. The workflow's dependency on run_loop.py makes it harder for subagents to complete successfully within time constraints.

5 of 30 total assertions discriminate in favor of with_skill. 1 assertion reverse-discriminates (eval 7 description change). The remaining 24 are non-discriminating. The +27pp delta is driven by a small number of highly specific assertions.
